question.worked_solution:
To solve compound "and" inequalities, we solve each inequality separately and then find their intersection.

- First, we solve $-18<10+7z<24\,:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-18 & <10+7z<24 \\ -18-10 & <10+7z-10<24-10 \\ -28 & <7z<14 \\ \frac{-28}{7} & <\frac{7z}{7}<\frac{14}{7} \\ -4 & <z<2\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14255803/assets/778e9b621c822549cdd15f68553596e6a4a53026588ad9832fdb251e7e851b02.png)

- Then, we solve $3z\ge -9\,:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3z & \ge -9 \\ \frac{3z}{3} & \ge \frac{-9}{3} \\ z & \ge -3\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14255803/assets/ad16a2201986ec6531d6dca654b74ca10f34bf6859e0275aea472364b7262800.png)

To find the values of $z$ that satisfy both inequalities, we find where the two solutions overlap:

![](@asset-2@)

Thus, the final solution is $-3\le z<2.$
